text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SWE-02: I extracted all 25 `sequence` and all 10 `fasta` fields programmatically. Seven distinct sequences account for 16 records, and every single line-number pairing the reviewer cites is exact: the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG at :153 (dG -16.2, Kd 2.1, pLDDT 94.8), :247 (-17.5, 0.65, 94.3) and :131 (-12.6, 92.8); the 41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC at :195 (α7 nAChR ECD), :319 (TLR4/MD-2) and :134; the 37-mer at :205/:361; the 31-mer at :173/:371; plus :163/:127, :215/:132, :225/:133. The 'same molecule, same receptor, different ΔG' point for drugs 2 and 11 (both AChE) is correct and is the strongest single argument in the finding. Thermodynamics re-derived with R=1.987204259e-3, T=298.15: RT=0.59248 (reviewer 0.5925, correct); ΔG=-18.4 implies Kd=3.256e-5 nM = 32.6 fM (reviewer 3.3e-5 nM, 33 fM, correct); Kd=0.32 nM implies ΔG=-12.95 (correct); 1 nM implies -12.28 (reviewer -12.27, correct to rounding). All 25 pairs violate the identity. Citation check: DOI 10.33011/livecoms.2.1.18378 resolves to Mey, Antonia S.J.S. et al., 'Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations [Article v1.0]', LiveCoMS 2, 2020 — real and correctly described. Correction: Four numerical errors and one substantive upgrade. (1) 'the pipeline contains 28 unique sequences across 35 records' — actual count is 26 unique across 35 (7 collisions absorbing 16 records, i.e. 9 excess). (2) 'pLDDT differs by up to 4.4 points' is wrong: the maximum spread on byte-identical input is 2.50 (drug 6 = 93.2, drug 18 = 92.8, candidate 10 = 90.7). The argument survives — 2.5 points is still far outside seed noise — but the figure must be corrected before issue. (3) 'ΔG by up to 4.4 kcal/mol' understates: the maximum is 4.90 (drug 2 -16.2, drug 11 -17.5, candidate 7 -12.6). (4) 'The discrepancy across all 25 records ranges from 3.45 to 5.73' — the true range is 3.85 to 5.73. (5) Substantive: the reviewer's inference that the numbers 'were written by hand' is under-argued and slightly wrong. I regressed ΔG on ln(Kd in M) across all 25 records: ΔG = 1.0495·ln(Kd_M) + 4.682 with R² = 0.994. They were not entered independently — they were generated by a single smooth rule with an effective RT of 1.05 kcal/mol (RT at ~528 K) plus a spurious +4.68 kcal/mol intercept. That is far stronger evidence than 'the offset is not constant' and it should replace that sentence.

text: The proposed fix for SWE-02 is NOT technically sufficient: Four numerical errors and one substantive upgrade. (1) 'the pipeline contains 28 unique sequences across 35 records' — actual count is 26 unique across 35 (7 collisions absorbing 16 records, i.e. 9 excess). (2) 'pLDDT differs by up to 4.4 points' is wrong: the maximum spread on byte-identical input is 2.50 (drug 6 = 93.2, drug 18 = 92.8, candidate 10 = 90.7). The argument survives — 2.5 points is still far outside seed noise — but the figure must be corrected before issue. (3) 'ΔG by up to 4.4 kcal/mol' understates: the maximum is 4.90 (drug 2 -16.2, drug 11 -17.5, candidate 7 -12.6). (4) 'The discrepancy across all 25 records ranges from 3.45 to 5.73' — the true range is 3.85 to 5.73. (5) Substantive: the reviewer's inference that the numbers 'were written by hand' is under-argued and slightly wrong. I regressed ΔG on ln(Kd in M) across all 25 records: ΔG = 1.0495·ln(Kd_M) + 4.682 with R² = 0.994. They were not entered independently — they were generated by a single smooth rule with an effective RT of 1.05 kcal/mol (RT at ~528 K) plus a spurious +4.68 kcal/mol intercept. That is far stronger evidence than 'the offset is not constant' and it should replace that sentence.

(1) app.js:381 `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` — confirmed prose, and confirmed reachable: openDrugModal (app.js:649-651) passes drug.sequence unconditionally to initModal3DCanvas, renderModalPlddtChart and renderModalPaeHeatmap, and currentActiveModalSequence (:600) is what copyModalFasta writes to the clipboard for the index.html:363 'Launch AlphaFold Server' button. (2) I enumerated non-standard residues across all 35 sequences: 'B' appears in exactly three records, at app.js:173, :371 and :130, and nowhere else — the reviewer's list is exact and complete. (4) app.js:50 ends `...C=C2)O)OCH3)O`; bare `CH3` is invalid SMILES because H is only legal inside brackets in the organic subset (B, C, N, O, S, P, F, Cl, Br, I) — the parse failure is a grammar consequence, not an empirical claim, so I accept it without running RDKit. Correction: None material. One presentational note: the pattern `^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$` proposed in the fix would reject the drug-24 prose record and all three B-containing records, exactly as claimed — I confirmed that by enumeration. This is the best-constructed finding in the set: every asserted defect is present, and each one is caught by the specific validator proposed.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SWE-04: Verified against `git ls-files`, not just the filesystem. The tracked artifact is exactly: .gitignore, README.md, app.js, index.html, skills-lock.json, styles.css, and .agents/skills/**. No package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, requirements.txt, Dockerfile, Makefile, LICENSE, CITATION.cff, CONTRIBUTING.md or paper.md at root; no tests/, .github/, data/, schemas/, src/ or docs/. `git tag -l` returns zero over five commits. README.md:119-124 reads verbatim as quoted, including `file:///Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html` — the absolute path and the OS username disclosure are real. The file:// point is technically right: Chrome and Safari treat file:// as an opaque origin and fail fetch(), so the documented launch method does foreclose external JSON loading. Citation 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285 verified: Sandve, Geir Kjetil, 'Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research', PLoS Comput Biol 9:e1003285, 2013. 10.3233/DS-210053 verified: Soiland-Reyes, Stian, 'Packaging research artefacts with RO-Crate', Data Science 5:97-138, 2022. Correction: Two. (1) 'no lockfile' and 'no dependency manifest of any kind' are wrong as stated: skills-lock.json is tracked, 10 KB, and is a content-hash-pinned lockfile (`computedHash` per skill, sourced from google-deepmind/science-skills), and .agents/skills carries a pyproject.toml plus PEP-723 inline dependency blocks. Scope the claim to 'no manifest or lockfile for the web application's own runtime dependencies', which remains true and is the point that matters. (2) The JOSS framing is a false standard and should be removed. The project was never submitted to JOSS, README.md:4 declares 'License-Private_Research', and the GitHub repository is private. 'Satisfies zero of the six and would be desk-rejected before a reviewer was assigned' measures the work against a venue its author never chose; it reads as manufactured severity and it is the sentence a defensive author will use to dismiss the whole report. The reproducibility argument stands entirely on its own without it.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SWE-05: The mechanism is real and I confirmed every link in it. `grep -n "dispose\|cancelAnimationFrame" app.js` returns exit 1 — neither token appears in the file. `grep -n "modalThreeRenderer"` shows the variable is declared at :410, assigned only at :688, and never set to null or undefined anywhere, so the guard `if (!modalThreeRenderer) return;` at :764 is permanently satisfied after the first modal open and no animation loop can ever terminate. closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) is three lines and does only `modal.classList.remove('active')`. Because animateModal3D closes over module-level globals rather than its own renderer, N surviving loops each mutate the same modalThreeMeshGroup, so rotation advances N × 0.006 rad/frame and render() is called N times per frame — the 2x-after-second-open prediction is correct. Geometry abandonment at :732, :742, :751, :757 with `container.innerHTML = ''` at :678 is confirmed. The Chart.js contrast at :779-781 is real and is a fair, well-observed point. Correction: Three. (1) The predicted user-visible symptom is wrong. 'A user who inspects all 25 candidates in one session will find the 3D panel dead for the last nine' is not supported — and is contradicted by the very warning the finding quotes, 'Too many active WebGL contexts. Oldest context will be lost.' Chrome evicts the least-recently-used context; modalThreeRenderer always points at the newest, so the visible panel keeps rendering. What the user actually observes is runaway rotation speed, linearly degrading frame time, and console warnings — not a blank panel. Fix the prediction or an author will refute the finding by opening 25 modals. (2) The finding misses the second, identical leak site: update3DProteinStructure (app.js:959-1022) empties proteinMeshGroup at :962-965 with remove() and no dispose(), then allocates a fresh TubeGeometry at :994 plus up to ceil(len/2) SphereGeometry meshes and MeshPhongMaterials at :1003-1010 on every leaderboard row click. Same defect class, not in the evidence list. (3) Cosmetic: 'grep returns exactly six lines' is followed by seven line numbers.

The npm registry gives three 0.128.0 published 2021-04-23T11:31:10Z and current latest 0.185.1 published 2026-07-01T14:04:30Z — so 'over five years behind' and '57 minor releases' (185 − 128) are both exact. Both three and chart.js report license MIT in registry metadata, so the vendoring recommendation is licensed correctly. `grep -c "integrity=" index.html` returns 0. No vendor/, lib/ or node_modules/ in the tree. index.html:11, :13, :15, :16, :18 are as described. The reproducibility argument — that no record anywhere in the repository pins the Chart.js version that produced the figures — is exactly right and is the part that matters more than the supply-chain half. Correction: One implementation caveat for whoever applies this, not an error in the finding: adding `crossorigin="anonymous"` and an SRI hash to the Google Fonts stylesheet at index.html:11 is not workable, because Google serves version-mutable CSS whose bytes change with the requesting user agent, so any integrity hash will intermittently fail closed and silently kill the page's typography. Vendor the font files instead, which the finding already recommends as the stronger endpoint. SRI hashes must also be generated per exact file path (chart.umd.min.js, not the bare package URL).

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SWE-07: Facts all verified. No LICENSE, LICENSE.md or COPYING at root (git ls-files confirms). README.md:3 is the shields.io badge with `logo=google` reading 'AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server'. index.html:30 subtitle is 'DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform'; :410 reads 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling'; :42 is the hyperlink-only 'Live Connected' pill. `grep -ri abramson` across all files returns nothing; no third-party attributions exist. I retrieved google-deepmind/alphafold3 OUTPUT_TERMS_OF_USE.md directly and every quoted clause is verbatim and correctly numbered: §1 non-commercial/permitted-organizations, §2 'To misinform, misrepresent or mislead' including 'misrepresenting your relationship with Google' and 'misrepresenting the origin of Output', §5 conspicuous notice, §6 the Abramson citation requirement, and the 'theoretical modeling only... not intended, validated, or approved for clinical use' disclaimer. Critically, the reviewer was careful and correct in attributing the automated-binding-prediction prohibition to the AlphaFold Server terms rather than to the GitHub Output terms — I confirmed it is absent from the GitHub file and present verbatim in the Server Output Terms via an independent mirror: 'IN CONNECTION WITH ANY AUTOMATED SYSTEM that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock.' The same source shows the misrepresentation clause expressly covers 'using Google's trademarks, trade names, logos or suggesting endorsement by Google', which lands squarely on the logo=google badge. Correction: One substantive reasoning error. The AlphaFold 3 Output Terms of Use govern Output. This project has produced, received and distributes zero AF3 Output, so §2, §5 and §6 do not attach to it, and the sentence '§6 requires citing Abramson; this project claims AlphaFold3 findings throughout and cites nothing' is not a breach of §6 — the defect is falsely claiming AF3 provenance, which is a different wrong. The claim that the conduct is 'aggravated, not mitigated, by the fact that no AlphaFold output is present at all' inverts the instrument: absence of Output removes the contract, it does not intensify it. Re-route the argument to what actually applies now: (i) ordinary trademark and passing-off exposure from placing 'DeepMind' and the Google logo in the masthead and badge of a third-party product, for which the Terms' own wording is strong evidence of how Google characterises the conduct rather than the operative prohibition; and (ii) a genuine §2/§5/§6 breach that becomes live the instant real Output enters the pipeline — which is why the fix's sequencing (resolve before building the compute layer) is right. Also: neither the reviewer nor I is counsel, and the finding should recommend counsel review rather than assert a violation. Severity stays CRITICAL on the independent grounds that the missing LICENSE makes lawful sharing impossible and that 'Live Connected' is a false statement of fact regardless of any contract.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on SWE-09: I re-derived every number rather than trusting the enumeration. Brute-forcing 93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (c%5)*0.5 over i in 1..200 and all uppercase c gives an exact range of [89.000, 99.000], so both clamps at app.js:792 (>100) and :793 (<70) are provably unreachable and the index.html:390-391 legend bands 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' describe unreachable states. With the y-axis fixed at min 50 (app.js:825), the data occupies 10 of 50 units — the '78% of the plot area is permanently empty' figure is exactly right. The residue-identity colouring at :747-749 is confirmed verbatim, so a proline is drawn amber (legended 'Low 50-70') in the 3D panel while the adjacent chart plots it at ≥89. PAE: maximum attainable is (gridSize-1)*0.4 + 3*0.3, which I computed as 18.5 Å at gridSize 45 and 11.7 Å for a 28-mer, so the :851 clamp is dead and the index.html:397 title '0 - 30 Å' overstates. Truncation: I checked all 25 sequence lengths and exactly one exceeds 45 — the 47-mer at app.js:143 — so precisely two residues are dropped silently, as claimed. Canvas is 540×220, ratio 2.4545:1. Every sub-claim holds. Correction: Two additions that are stronger than anything currently in the finding and should be folded in. (1) The generated PAE diagonal is nonzero: PAE[i][i] takes values {0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9} Å depending on the residue's ASCII code, whereas a real PAE matrix is identically zero on the diagonal by definition. That is a one-line check and it is the single most conclusive internal proof that this is not a PAE matrix. (2) The matrix is asymmetric in a way no PAE generator produces — PAE[0][5]=2.90 vs PAE[5][0]=2.00 for the drug-2 sequence — because the ASCII term keys on the row index only. Severity MINOR is correct given SWE-01 subsumes the panels, but the finding's real value is as the cheapest available evidence that nobody ever compared these figures against a genuine AlphaFold output, and that framing should lead it.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: Two of the 'de novo designed' molecules are verbatim wild-type sequence. Drug 14 BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 (app.js:277) and candidate rank 5 CogAbeta-Clearer-08 (app.js:129) both begin KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, which is exactly Aβ(16-35) of human amyloid-beta (Aβ42 = DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA; positions 16–35 match character for character). KLVFFAE is the amyloidogenic nucleation core. So an 'Aβ fibril disruptor' and an 'Aβ clearer' are each built on the aggregation nucleus of the peptide they claim to clear, presented without comment. More generally the sequences are known literature motifs (Nrf2 ETGE as DEETGE, Wnt/Fzd and Trk fragments) concatenated with GGGGS linkers — which contradicts 'designed via AlphaFold3' independently of whether AF3 was ever run, and needs no structure prediction to establish. SWE-02 sorted these sequences for duplication and never asked what they were.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The README ADMET claims flagged in the brief are never addressed on their substance. README:96-102 and the per-drug safety strings assert things no in silico method can emit: 'IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)' — no predictor outputs a zero risk; 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' — a 30-day longitudinal receptor-regulation endpoint is an in vivo measurement, not a static-model output, and nothing in this codebase computes anything over time; and 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (:281), 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%' (:375). SWE-03 touches app.js:147 only as a string-formatting problem. Absolute 0% and 100% safety claims on a self-described drug discovery platform are the numbers most likely to be quoted out of the artifact and they deserved their own finding.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The remediation is far cheaper than the review's 'rewrite along a three-layer boundary' implies, because the tooling is already committed to this repository. `git ls-files` shows .agents/skills/alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze/scripts/ containing fetch_structure.py — which pulls real mmCIF and PAE JSON from https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/api/prediction/{uniprot_id} — plus analyze_plddt.py and analyze_pae.py, Apache-2.0, sourced from google-deepmind/science-skills and hash-pinned in the tracked skills-lock.json. The reviewer both asserted AlphaFold is 'never even contacted' anywhere and declared 'no lockfile' while this was in the index. A reviewer who misses what is already in the tree mis-scopes the effort estimate, and effort estimates are what determine whether an author acts on a report or discards it.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The benchmark chart plots two incommensurate units on one shared axis. app.js:1057-1102 renders a dimensionless 0–100 index (CEI) and |ΔG| in kcal/mol as two bar series against a single untitled linear y-axis, so the ΔG bars are compressed to roughly a fifth of the CEI bars purely by unit choice while the chart invites direct visual comparison between them. For a review whose declared discipline covers scientific data presentation, a two-unit single-axis bar chart on the artifact's only summary figure is a standard finding.
